title: Iterated localization coherence
statement:
Localizing first at $s$ and then at $t$ gives the same graded equivalence as
localizing at $st$, after the canonical equivalence
$(A_s)_t\cong A_{st}$.

proof.text:
Both maps send a homogeneous coefficient $x\in I^n$ to $x/1$ and commute
with the inclusions of the localized base ring. Graded ring-homomorphism
extensionality gives equality.

**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the affine blow-up and its

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $s,t\in A$. Localizing the Rees algebra first at $s$ and then at the
image of $t$ gives the same graded ring homomorphism as localizing at $st$,
after the canonical isomorphism $(A_s)_t\cong A_{st}$: the composite
$\mathcal R_A(I)\to\mathcal R_{A_s}(IA_s)\to\mathcal R_{(A_s)_t}(I(A_s)_t)
\to\mathcal R_{A_{st}}(IA_{st})$ of coefficientwise maps equals
$\rho_{st}$. Consequently the same holds for the induced morphisms of
affine blow-ups.

proof.text:
Coefficientwise maps compose like the underlying ring homomorphisms:
applying $\varphi$ and then $\psi$ to every coefficient is applying
$\psi\varphi$. The composite $A\to A_s\to(A_s)_t\to A_{st}$ is the
localization map $A\to A_{st}$, so the composite of the three
coefficientwise maps is $\rho_{st}$; both send a homogeneous coefficient
$x\in I^n$ to $x/1$. The morphisms of affine blow-ups are induced by
these graded homomorphisms on Proj, contravariantly and compatibly with
composition, which gives the second statement.
